subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, Philosophy of the skill, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and current web-platform dark-mode primitives (prefers-color-scheme, color-scheme, light-dark(), pre-paint script, <picture> media, meta theme-color, persistence with explicit-over-system).

cases.scenario: A React SSR app applies the persisted theme in a useEffect after hydration. Dark-mode users see a clear white flash on every cold load before the dark theme kicks in.
cases.context: The app is server-rendered and reads no theme on the server; the toggle writes to localStorage.
cases.question: How should the agent eliminate the flash?
expected_flags: useEffect runs after first paint — too late; the light default already painted
Add a blocking inline script in <head> that reads the persisted preference and sets a class/data-attribute on <html> before stylesheets resolve
For SSR, serialize the resolved theme into the HTML response by reading a cookie on the server
Verify by throttling the network and watching the first paint
expected_fix_hints: Move theme resolution to a pre-paint inline <head> script
Persist via cookie so the server can serialize the theme into the initial HTML
absent_signals: Do not apply the theme in useEffect / after hydration
Do not leave the default light theme painting first

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: useEffect runs after first paint — too late; the light default already painted.

Surfaces this expected flag: For SSR, serialize the resolved theme into the HTML response by reading a cookie on the server.
Surfaces this expected flag: Verify by throttling the network and watching the first paint.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Move theme resolution to a pre-paint inline <head> script.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Persist via cookie so the server can serialize the theme into the initial HTML.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not apply the theme in useEffect / after hydration.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not leave the default light theme painting first.

cases.scenario: A toggle only has a single light/dark switch. A user on a dark-OS who picked Light on the site keeps getting Dark again whenever the page reloads, because the app re-reads prefers-color-scheme each time.
cases.context: The product should respect both the OS and an explicit override.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the preference model?
expected_flags: Offer three states: System, Light, Dark — not a single two-way switch
Persist the explicit choice (localStorage/cookie) and have it override the OS preference
System is a distinct third state that defers to prefers-color-scheme
On load, read the persisted choice first; fall back to the media query only when System (or nothing) is set
expected_fix_hints: Store {system|light|dark} and resolve at load with explicit-over-system precedence
Add the System option as a real choice
absent_signals: Do not re-derive from prefers-color-scheme when an explicit choice exists
Do not collapse System into 'no preference'

Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not collapse System into 'no preference'.

cases.scenario: Dark mode works for app content, but native form controls (checkboxes, date pickers, scrollbars) and the default page background still render light, looking out of place in dark mode.
cases.context: The site supports both light and dark schemes.
cases.question: What should the agent add?
expected_flags: Declare the CSS color-scheme property on :root with the supported schemes (e.g. color-scheme: light dark)
color-scheme tells the user agent which schemes the page supports so native controls/scrollbars/default background render correctly
Keep it in sync with the active theme (or set both with the data-attribute approach)
This is a platform integration a CSS-only re-skin misses
expected_fix_hints: Add color-scheme to :root and align it with the resolved theme
Let the UA theme native controls instead of restyling each one
absent_signals: Do not try to hand-restyle every native control instead of using color-scheme

cases.scenario: In dark mode, the company logo (a dark wordmark on a transparent background) is invisible in the header and the browser tab, and hero illustrations with white backgrounds glare against the dark page.
cases.context: Assets are a mix of raster PNGs, an SVG logo, and a favicon.
cases.question: How should the agent handle the assets?
expected_flags: Raster brand-color images: provide dark variants via <picture> with <source media=(prefers-color-scheme: dark)> or CSS background swapping
SVG logo: use currentColor or CSS custom properties for fill/stroke so it adapts automatically
Favicon: declare a dark variant via <link rel=icon media=(prefers-color-scheme: dark)>
Dark mode is a parallel design surface — assets need real variants, not just inverted colors
expected_fix_hints: Author dark asset variants and wire them by media query
Make the SVG theme-aware via currentColor/custom properties
absent_signals: Do not leave a single light-only logo/favicon
Do not CSS-invert photos as the fix

cases.scenario: On mobile, the browser address bar stays white in dark mode, creating a jarring light band above the dark page; the installed PWA splash also mismatches.
cases.context: The site supports light and dark and is installable as a PWA.
cases.question: What should the agent add?
expected_flags: Add meta theme-color with paired light and dark variants via media= so the chrome matches the active theme
theme-color sets the mobile address bar color, Safari toolbar tint, and PWA splash
Keep both variants so each scheme gets the right chrome color
Note apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style is overridden by theme-color on supported versions
expected_fix_hints: Add <meta name=theme-color> with light and dark media variants
Match theme-color to the resolved theme's surface color
absent_signals: Do not ship a single theme-color that mismatches one scheme
Do not omit the dark variant

cases.scenario: A PM asks the dark-mode-implementation owner to design the actual dark color palette, pick the dark surface and text values, and verify they pass WCAG AA — and also to architect a five-brand white-label theming system.
cases.context: The team conflates 'dark mode' with all color and theming work.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Choosing the dark palette values and verifying their contrast is color-system-design (and a11y for the criteria), not this skill
A five-brand multi-theme architecture is theme-system-design, not the two-state dark case
Offer the in-scope part: wiring detection/persistence/flash-prevention/assets/chrome once the palette exists
Correctly redirects rather than designing colors or a multi-theme architecture
expected_fix_hints: Hand palette/contrast to color-system-design and the multi-theme architecture to theme-system-design
Implement the runtime switch over the resulting tokens
absent_signals: Do not pick the dark palette values here
Do not architect a five-theme system in this skill

cases.scenario: After a CSS-only dark theme, cards rely on drop shadows that disappear on the dark background, focus rings are barely visible, and chart colors that read well on white wash out on dark.
cases.context: The toggle and tokens already work; the dark mode just feels half-finished.
cases.question: How should the agent finish the dark surface?
expected_flags: Dark mode is a parallel design surface, not a re-skin
Replace shadows with subtle borders or elevated background tints on dark
Ensure focus rings and other interactive states are visible and contrast-compliant in dark
Rework chart palettes for the dark surface; verify visually and with automated contrast testing
expected_fix_hints: Swap shadow strategy for elevation tints/borders in dark
Re-tune focus-ring and chart colors for the dark surface
absent_signals: Do not assume the same shadows/focus/chart colors work on dark
Do not treat dark as done after the color overrides
